account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers and humans and transmit only images of interest. Researchers and forest department officials received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim. The cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources. The original paper reports that forest officials sent text-chat warnings to village leaders after detections that concerned them, although these messages were not rapid. The sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict.

ai_role.statement: Embedded AI selected and transmitted tiger and human images within 30–42 seconds. Forest officials then informed village leaders by text chat about detections that concerned them, although the study says that these messages were not rapid. The sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict.

fields.account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers and humans and transmit only images of interest. Researchers and forest department officials received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim. The cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources. The original paper reports that forest officials sent text-chat warnings to village leaders after detections that concerned them, although these messages were not rapid. The sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict.
